I am 74 years old and have farmed these fields in Quzhou County since I was a young girl. My family has always grown winter wheat followed by summer corn on this land — that is what the North China Plain gives us, and that is what my hands know. I have no schooling, but I have sixty years of watching the weather and working this soil. At my age, I will not gamble with new crops or fancy methods I do not trust. I farm four mu of land that my family has tended for generations. I will plant improved wheat seeds in the autumn after turning the soil with the rotary tiller, because the ground needs loosening after the corn stalks. I will spread fertilizer the way I always have — not too little and not so much that it wastes money — and I will water three times: once before the cold sets in, once when the wheat greens up in spring, and once when the grain is filling. When the wheat comes off in early June, I will immediately put in hybrid corn seed using no-tillage, because there is no time to waste between crops and my back is not what it used to be. I will irrigate the corn twice if the summer rains are stingy, and I will spray when the bugs come, just enough to keep the plants healthy. This rotation has always given us flour for the household, feed for the chickens, and cash from the grain buyer. I do not need surprises. I need steady food and a little money to get through the year.
